Verticillium Wilt (bottom-left reference) shows very similar extensive brown necrosis with yellowing — close match. Let me check a couple more.

- **Test image**: Severely wilted, papery-dry leaf; extensive brown necrosis across most of the leaf surface; residual green near main veins; visible yellowing patches; no discrete circular spots, no webbing, no powdery coating.

- **Eliminations**:
  - Early_Blight: distinct concentric ring spots — not present
  - Late_Blight: dark purple-brown blotches on still-green leaves — doesn't match
  - Powdery_Mildew: white powdery coating — not visible
  - Target_Spot: mostly-green leaves with small pinpoint spots — not matching
  - Leaf_Mold: olive-colored spores on underside, pale yellow spots — not matching
  - Spider_Mites: stippling/webbing — not present

- **Best match — Verticillium_Wilt**: The Verticillium Wilt reference (bottom-left panel) shows the same pattern: extensive brown-dried necrosis with yellowing and residual green near veins. The description says lower leaves die with brown necrotic tissue, which matches the almost-completely-dead appearance of this leaf.
